classification.difficultyReason: Construct tangent sightlines, relate a central angle to the visible circumference, and reverse the calculation for a specified percentage.

content.prompt: Tom stands $2\text{ m}$ from a cylindrical silo of radius $5\text{ m}$.

spec.description: Unfilled circular silo cross-section with a radial segment continuing to Tom on the right. Tangent sightlines are absent from the student figure.
spec.mathematics: Radius 5 m; Tom is 2 m beyond the boundary along the radius, so his distance from the centre is 7 m.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions and point T are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the percentage of the silo that he can see, correct to the nearest whole percentage.

answer.short:
$25\%$.

The tangent sightlines bound the visible arc.
answer.worked:
Let $O$ be the centre and $A$ a point where a sightline from $T$ touches the silo. Since a tangent is perpendicular to the radius, $\triangle OAT$ is right-angled at $A$. Let $\theta=\angle AOT$, measured in radians.
$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{5}{7}\\\theta&=\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{5}{7}\right).\end{align*}$$
The two tangent sightlines bound a visible arc with central angle $2\theta$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Visible percentage}&=\frac{2\theta}{2\pi}\times100\%\\\text{Visible percentage}&=\frac{100}{\pi}\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{5}{7}\right)\%\\\text{Visible percentage}&\approx24.68\%\\\text{Visible percentage}&\approx25\%\quad\text{(nearest whole percentage).}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the distance from the silo (to the nearest metre) that Tom should stand so that he can see $40\%$ of the silo.

answer.short:
$11\text{ m}$ from the silo.

Use half the visible central angle in the right triangle formed by a radius and a tangent sightline.
answer.worked:
Let $d$ metres be Tom's distance from the silo and $\theta$ half the visible central angle, in radians.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2\theta}{2\pi}&=0.4\\\theta&=\frac{2\pi}{5}.\end{align*}$$
The tangent sightline is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
$$\begin{align*}\cos\!\left(\frac{2\pi}{5}\right)&=\frac{5}{5+d}\\5+d&=\frac{5}{\cos(2\pi/5)}\\d&=\frac{5}{\cos(2\pi/5)}-5\\d&\approx11.18\text{ m}\\d&\approx11\text{ m}\quad\text{(nearest metre).}\end{align*}$$
